recipe_version.title: Moroccan Chickpea Skillet
recipe_version.description: Chickpeas with ras el hanout, preserved-lemon rind, and spinach, served over couscous.
recipe_version.doneness: Chickpeas glossy, skillet not soupy. Spinach just wilted. Couscous tender and separate, not mush.

substitutions.couscous: This version uses wheat couscous. A gluten-free stand-in would change the allergen list and is not this version.
substitutions.preserved lemon: Rind only. Do not chop in the salty pulp, and do not swap in fresh lemon wedges.

ingredients.name: preserved lemon
ingredients.note: chopped rind only; rinse and discard the pulp. Store-bought jarred preserved lemon.

ingredients.name: couscous
ingredients.note: dry wheat couscous, not a gluten-free substitute

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: divided: 1 1/2 cups boiling water for the couscous, 1/4 cup in the skillet. v1 said only a splash.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: in the couscous only. Diamond Crystal. If Morton, use 1/4 tsp. Do not salt the skillet; the preserved lemon is already salty.

steps.title: Steam the couscous
steps.body: Put the dry couscous and the kosher salt in a bowl. Pour over 1 1/2 cups boiling water. Cover and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. This is wheat couscous for all 4 servings. v1 said only for serving.

steps.title: Spice the chickpeas
steps.body: Warm the neutral oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the ras el hanout and cook 1 minute. Add the drained chickpeas and 1/4 cup water. Cook 5 minutes, until the chickpeas are glossy and the water is mostly gone.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: Stir in the preserved-lemon rind and the spinach. Cook 1-2 minutes, until the spinach is just wilted and the skillet is not soupy. Do not add more salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Serve the skillet over the couscous. Four servings.

projection.vocabulary_note: Dropped v1 tag curries. This is a skillet with a splash of water, not a curry. Kept citrusy because preserved lemon is in the dish.
projection.allergen_note: Wheat comes from the couscous. It is an allergen, not a dietary tag. Dietary eligibility stays plant and dairy-free. Gluten-free is not claimed.
